clue.text: Gold armour regularly put on a fairytale princess

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A princess in a fairy tale is dressed in golden armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' reads as dressing the princess, but it simply places the pieces next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora is the name of Sleeping Beauty in the Disney film and some ballet versions of the story.

clue.text: Financially supported Spooner's arrant daring

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words

parts.note: arrant and rank both mean utter, as in an arrant fool; it takes the opening sound of the next word
a bold move is a daring one; it takes the opening sound of the previous word

explanation.surface: Someone recklessly brave was paid for by a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: RANK BOLD with its first sounds exchanged becomes BANK ROLLED.
explanation.definitionFit: To bankroll a venture is to provide the money behind it, so bankrolled means paid for or funded.

clue.text: Trailers for comic drama Groundhog Day giving little away

indicators.note: a trailer comes at the back, so each word gives up its final letter

parts.note: the final letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Film trailers for the comedy Groundhog Day reveal very little of the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailers' looks like film advertising, but it asks for the tail letters of the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagy person is guarded and secretive, unwilling to reveal information.

clue.text: Obnoxious detectives held up Sikh wrongly

indicators.note: in a down entry, holding something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

indicators.note: letters put down wrongly are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Unpleasant police officers stopped a Sikh man without good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' suggests a robbery or delay, but in a down clue it turns the detectives upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickish is informal slang for behaving like a jerk, so rude and unpleasant.

clue.text: Nonlinear narrative holds merit

indicators.note: a phrase that holds something keeps it inside, here a run of letters spanning two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A story told out of chronological order has its own worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merit' looks like a noun after 'holds', but it is the verb: to deserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn something is to deserve it by your efforts, just as to merit it.

clue.text: Kid catches Labradors climbing for fun on table

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it, so one word wraps round another

parts.note: to kid someone is to fool them

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing goes from the bottom upwards, turning the word round

parts.note: Labs is the usual short form for Labrador retrievers

explanation.surface: A child grabs the dogs as they scramble up onto the table for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' reads as a child, but it is the verb meaning to tease or deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: Foosball is table football, a game played for amusement on a table with rods and little figures.

clue.text: Thickener helping you finally blot a pen

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so each of the two words gives only its closing letter

parts.note: the last letters of the two words
to blot or mar is to spoil or stain
taken as written
Bic is a well-known brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: Someone thickening a sauce is told to use a pen as a final step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a portion of food, but only its last letter is used, with that of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum arabic is a natural resin from acacia trees, used in food as a stabiliser and thickening agent.

clue.text: Laugh, professor being tricked

parts.note: the sound of a laugh
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: People laugh as an academic falls for a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a British university lecturer. To have someone on is British slang for teasing or deceiving them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being had on means being fooled or kidded, a British idiom equivalent to being tricked.

clue.text: Seeing China, cycled over mostly dirt

indicators.note: one thing laid over another covers it, so the outer word spreads across the inner one
going round a cycle moves letters from the front round to the back
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
smut is dirt or soot, as well as indecent material

explanation.surface: A traveller tours China by bicycle over dirt roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing' looks like sightseeing in China, but it is the conjunction meaning since. Moving the first two letters to the back is what 'cycled' asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing and inasmuch (as) both introduce a reason, meaning considering that or since.

clue.text: Athlete Jay subs for Henry in team sport

indicators.note: a sub replaces a player, so one letter comes on and another goes off

parts.note: jay is the spoken name of the letter J
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
hockey is played by two teams

explanation.surface: A sportsman called Jay comes on as a substitute for Henry in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Jay and Henry look like player names, but they are the letters J and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey rides racehorses professionally, and is a sportsman in a demanding physical sport.

clue.text: Family returned post shilling for charity

parts.note: kin are relatives

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
s was the abbreviation for the shilling, an old British coin worth twelve pence

explanation.surface: Relatives sent a shilling back in the mail as a donation to a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' seems to describe the family, but it acts on the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity in its older sense is benevolence and goodwill towards others, which is kindness.

clue.text: Some flaws in translation besetting over five Bible books

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so one part closes round another
translating turns words into a different form, so the letters are rewritten in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A few errors creep into a translation of the opening books of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a vague quantity, but it belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Law of Moses, or Torah, is the traditional name for the Pentateuch, the first five books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Second theatrical award includes concerning lack of diversity

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so a small word goes inside another

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
on means about, concerning
the Tony is the top American award for Broadway theatre

explanation.surface: Critics complain that a second stage prize again rewards the same kind of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal, but it is a short moment of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotony is sameness and a tedious absence of variety, so a want of variation.

clue.text: Orderly thanks nurse upon retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly thanks a nurse when she retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' reads as a hospital porter, but it is the adjective for tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neat is tidy and in good order, so the adjective sense of orderly fits.

clue.text: Ladies in denial squandered warning

parts.note: saying no is a denial
to blow money is to waste it
an omen is a sign warning of what is to come

explanation.surface: Some women refuse to accept they ignored a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In denial' reads as a psychological state, but 'in' is only a link and 'denial' gives its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies in the title sense are women of the aristocracy, the wives and daughters of peers.

clue.text: Work uniform temporarily provided with deep pockets

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work of music
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
something lent is provided only for a time

explanation.surface: Staff are lent work clothing with big pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep pockets' looks like part of the uniform's design, but it is the idiom for wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with deep pockets has plenty of money, and opulent means wealthy and lavish.

clue.text: Conditions for mayday met by Victoria

parts.note: pro means in favour of
the first two letters of the name, its familiar short form Vi
both are distress calls

explanation.surface: Someone sending a distress call is answered by a woman named Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a preposition linking the definition, but it supplies the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a clause in an agreement that makes it depend on a stated condition.

clue.text: Objection from beginners ignored by explosive expert

indicators.note: ignoring the beginners means leaving out the opening letter of each word

parts.note: a squib is a small firework
an able person is skilled

explanation.surface: A bomb-disposal expert overrules a protest from trainees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive expert' looks like a single person, but the two words each lose their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A quibble is a petty objection or criticism over a trivial point.

clue.text: Slav from Ljubljana is survivor after uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising up makes the letters read from the bottom upwards
taken from within the words, as a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the end of the city name, the whole middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A Slovene from the capital is the one left alive after a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Ljubljana is the capital of Slovenia, which makes 'Slav' look like a description of a Slovene.
explanation.definitionFit: Russians are the largest of the Slavic peoples of eastern Europe.

clue.text: Betrayed spouse, principally with ex

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or first of all, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letter of the word
ex as a prefix means former, so old

explanation.surface: A husband or wife was cheated on, mainly with a former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Betrayed' looks like being cheated on, but it is the sense of being sold out.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone, or sell them out, is to betray them for gain.

clue.text: Cheat ultimately regrets hesitations, means to stop lying

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of the word
ruth is an old word for pity or regret, as in ruthless
er and um are two sounds of hesitation

explanation.surface: A liar is finally sorry and stammers about ways to give up the habit.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'hesitations' hints that two separate hesitation noises are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A truth serum is a drug supposed to make someone speak honestly, so it ends their deceit.

clue.text: Country sounds of sheep and fowl

indicators.note: sounds point to how words are heard, not how they are written

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep
a gander is a male goose

explanation.surface: Rural noises of farm animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' suggests the countryside, but it is a nation; in a non-rhotic British accent GANDER loses its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is a nation in East Africa.

clue.text: Chances to see contest to get theatre parts

parts.note: to vie is to compete
the wings are the side areas of a stage

explanation.surface: Actors compete for roles in a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre parts' suggests roles in a play, but it means physical areas of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewings are occasions to look at something, such as a house for sale or a film screening.

clue.text: Audibly process dairy product

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: a way of doing something is a process or method

explanation.surface: Instructions read out on how to treat milk products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Process' looks like a verb about making dairy food, but it is the noun meaning method.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the watery liquid left after milk curdles in cheesemaking.

clue.text: Very hard times written about by a North African

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters are written in the opposite order

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
H is hard, as on pencils
x is the multiplication sign
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An account of very difficult times written by someone from North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North African' looks like the definition, but North only supplies a letter: the Xhosa people live in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Xhosan describes the Xhosa, a people of the Eastern Cape in South Africa, so it is an African term.

clue.text: I'm after whiskey shot that goes right through one

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for X follows Whiskey for W

definitions.text: shot that goes right through one
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a medical image made by radiation that passes through the body

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a drinker after a whiskey chaser; 'shot' is a photograph, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The NATO code word for the letter after W also names a radiograph, a picture taken through a patient's body.

clue.text: Provincial couple head for London

parts.note: to yoke is to couple or join together

indicators.note: the head is the top, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the city name

explanation.surface: A pair from the country set off for the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head for' looks like travelling towards the city, but it picks out an initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Provincial as a noun means a person from outside the capital, and a yokel is an unsophisticated country dweller.

clue.text: Spanish dance to finish off a tea party

parts.note: to zap is to kill or destroy
taken as written
a do is a party, so a tea do

explanation.surface: A dance in the Spanish style rounds off an afternoon gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is informal British for a party or social function.
explanation.definitionFit: The zapateado is a flamenco-style Spanish dance marked by rhythmic stamping of the heels.
